content: We praise a man who feels angry on the right grounds and against the right persons, and also in the right manner and at the right moment and for the right length of time.
author: Aristotle
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Holding onto anger is like clutching a glowing coal with the intent of throwing it at someone else—you are the one who gets burned. Retaliation only ties you tighter to the person who harmed you.

Across his life and work, Aristotle saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Forgiveness and composure are not signs of weakness or giving someone a pass. They are acts of fierce self-preservation, cutting the emotional chain that allows another person's bad behavior to ruin your peace of mind.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
